title: China's suspension of its gallium/germanium/antimony/superhard-materials export ban to the US runs out (MOFCOM, Announcement 46 of 2024 Article 2)
source: NEWS: MOFCOM Announcement No. 72 of 2025 (2025-11-09) suspended Article 2 of Announcement No. 46 of 2024 'until November 27, 2026' (Fastmarkets, Engineering News, The Star, all 2025-11; Mondaq/Clark Hill, Global Trade Alert summaries; nami-ts 2026-10-22 quotes the operative sentence). The 2026-11-09 MOFCOM/GAC notice (reported as No. 58 of 2026) keeps the six October-2025 measures suspended to 2027-01-10 and, per Skillings (2026-11-09), 'does not mention Announcement No. 72 and does not extend that suspension'. One trade-press source; MOFCOM text unread (english.mofcom.gov.cn resets the connection). Filed estimate: press-reported, no primary text.
notes: A SEPARATE CLOCK FROM THE 2027-01-10 ONE. A lapse restores only the US-specific in-principle ban (and stricter US-bound graphite review); worldwide licensing on the three metals has applied since 2023/2024 and never lapsed, and the ban on dual-use exports to US military users is untouched either way. Initial research 2026-11-12 stands aside: the tape cannot price a clock this narrow, there are no keyed symbols, and 11/27 is the half-day after Thanksgiving. Dates are estimates; research only; an estimate widens caution and never licenses a position.
